los.text: Perform an examination of the male genitalia with increased confidence and appropriate clinical technique.
los.html:
• Male genital and groin examination: see ICM Year 1 › Reproductive & sexual health › LO 10. "Increased confidence": clear explanation
    • chaperone
    • standing and lying
    • systematic palpation of both testes
    • epididymis and cords
    • transillumination
    • hernial orifices with cough
    • inguinal nodes
    • dignity throughout.

los.text: Perform an examination of the ear, nose and throat with increased confidence and appropriate clinical technique.
los.html:
• ENT examination: see ICM Year 1 › Eyes & ENT › LO 1.
    • Focus on correct otoscope technique (largest comfortable speculum, pull the pinna up and back, steady hand braced on the cheek), Rinne's and Weber's interpretation, and a quick systematic throat and neck exam.

los.text: Perform simple interrupted suturing on a model or in a clinical setting.
los.html:
1Check the wound (clean, <12–24 h, no foreign body, no tendon/nerve injury, not a bite needing delayed closure), consent, tetanus status.
2Clean, local anaesthetic, irrigate, sterile field and gloves.
3. Needle holderGrasp the needle two-thirds from the tip; toothed forceps to evert the edge.
4
  • Enter at 90° to the skin
  • ~3–5 mm from the edge
  • Follow the curve of the needle
  • Exit the same distance on the other side at the same depth.
5. Instrument tieDouble throw then two single throws (surgeon's knot), knot to one side; cut ends ~5 mm.
6Space sutures ~5–10 mm apart; evert edges, don't strangle (swelling).
7Dressing; advise on wound care; removal time: face 3–5 days, scalp 7–10, trunk and arms 7–10, legs and feet 10–14.
Suture materialUse
Non-absorbable (nylon/prolene)Skin closure
Absorbable (Vicryl, Monocryl)Deep layers, subcuticular, mouth
SizeFace 5-0/6-0, limbs and trunk 3-0/4-0

los.text: Describe the indications, types, and safe administration of local anaesthetics.
los.html:
Local anaestheticMax dose (plain)With adrenalineOnset / duration
Lidocaine3 mg/kg (max 200 mg)7 mg/kg (max 500 mg)Fast / 1–2 h
Bupivacaine2 mg/kg (max 150 mg)2 mg/kgSlow / 4–8 h
  • 1% = 10 mg/mL (e.g. 20 mL of 1% lidocaine = 200 mg).
  • Adrenaline prolongs action and reduces bleeding
    • traditionally avoided in digits, nose, penis, ears (end arteries), though evidence now suggests it's safe in fingers.
  • Safe administration: check allergy and weight
    • calculate the max dose
    • aspirate before injecting (avoid IV)
    • inject slowly through wound edges
    • wait for effect (test sensation).
  • Toxicity (LAST): perioral tingling, metallic taste, tinnitus, lightheadedness → seizures → arrhythmias, cardiac arrest
    • stop, ABCDE, call for help, lipid emulsion (Intralipid 20%).
